title: AgentOS Runtime Foundation Task Plan
objective: Implement the bottom Agent Core Runtime and harden the AgentOS Security Execution Foundation so the future distribution has a real agent control plane rather than hand-written workflows.
assumptions: The completed Linux MVP safety substrate remains the baseline and must not be bypassed.
Agent Core is deterministic orchestration around model output, not the model itself.
ModelBroker starts with a stub provider and must support local-only execution.
External LLM usage remains optional and cannot be required by acceptance tests.
Service recovery remains the first migration workflow because it already exercises diagnostics, approval, audit, and verification.
Distribution Alpha is blocked until this workflow proves a generic Agent run loop.

waves.name: Runtime Boundary Freeze
waves.purpose: Define the contract between Agent Core Runtime and the Security Execution Foundation before implementation starts.
exit_criteria: AgentCore, ModelBroker, Memory, Planner, Scheduler, Policy, Capability, Audit, Rollback, and Recovery ownership is explicit.
Plan and effect state transitions are written as deterministic contracts.
No module can directly execute model-generated text.
Security substrate invariants from the MVP are preserved.

waves.name: Agent Core Contracts
waves.purpose: Create the typed data model and model abstraction needed by a real Agent runtime.
exit_criteria: IntentCtx, PlanSpec, PlanStep, PlanRun, Observation, and RunState are versioned and serializable.
ModelBroker trait can serve stub/local providers with bounded, structured outputs.
Planner can produce a frozen PlanSpec without side effects.
Risk hints are advisory only and policy remains authoritative.

waves.name: Security Execution Foundation Hardening
waves.purpose: Turn the MVP safety substrate into a reusable execution foundation for all Agent plans.
exit_criteria: Every effect has a transaction envelope from prepare to seal or rollback.
Policy and capability checks are reusable by generic Agent steps.
Sandbox profiles are derived from leases and cannot be weakened by planner output.
Secret handles have explicit lease and redaction rules.

waves.name: Generic Agent Run Loop
waves.purpose: Implement the deterministic loop that schedules, executes, observes, verifies, and persists Agent runs.
exit_criteria: PlanRun can advance through Accepted, Planned, AwaitingApproval, Executing, Verifying, Completed, Suspended, and RollbackPending.
Step scheduling honors dependencies and risk gates.
Observation processing cannot create direct tool execution.
Run memory persists useful context while excluding secret values.
Crash recovery can reconstruct an in-flight run.

waves.name: Workflow Migration and Safety Gates
waves.purpose: Prove the generic runtime by migrating service recovery and adding adversarial gates.
exit_criteria: Service recovery uses the generic Agent run loop rather than a dedicated orchestration path.
Prompt injection, observation injection, memory poisoning, approval bypass, and tool abuse regressions fail closed.
Audit timeline shows intent, plan, policy decisions, leases, effects, observations, verification, and final summary.
The release gate can distinguish runtime failures from model-planning failures.

waves.name: Distribution Readiness Bridge
waves.purpose: Define the handoff from runtime foundation to the future AgentOS distribution workflow.
exit_criteria: Distribution Alpha entry criteria are updated to require Agent Core Runtime completion.
The runtime foundation has a final audit with tests, QEMU smoke where applicable, and no tracked generated artifacts.
